newsitem.title: UK: "Middle England" poll shows falling Tory support.
newsitem.headline: "Middle England" poll shows falling Tory support.

text.p: A poll of Mail on Sunday readers -- considered the crucial group that Labour needs to win over to secure victory in the May 1 election -- has shown a huge drop in support for the Conservative Party since 1992.
A MORI On-Line poll of the newspaper's 1,008-strong readers panel put the Conservatives on 49 points (down one from last month), Labour on 37 (up one), and the Liberal Democrats steady on 10.
The newspaper said that compared with how the same readers voted in 1992 -- when the Conservatives had a 41-point lead -- it amounts to a "collapse" in support for the government.

However, fear of what a Labour government would do in office has increased, with half the panel now saying they are fearful of Labour (45 percent last month), and only 38 percent were on balance hopeful.
The Mail on Sunday poll said 75 percent of those polled agree that "Britain needs a fresh team of leaders".
But four in 10 converts to Labour are not fully committed, and half those who have defected from the Tories since 1992 may change their minds.

The Mail on Sunday said the panel was from its readership which matched the characteristics of Middle England -- with more homeowners, second car owners and, traditionally, more Conservative voters than any other Sunday paper.
